label: Life expectancy at birth
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = UN DYB Table 4, national official statistics as reported, 12 editions, 2007-2024, sex-split (Male/Female) as printed by the collector; witness tier = OWID "life expectancy" (UN WPP estimates and historical reconstructions — Riley, HMD — both sexes), near-global, longer span (to 1875 for some entities). Authenticity first per ADR-0008: displayed beside each other, never blended.
license: Mixed, per source (see "sources"): UN DYB = UN data reuse policy (attribution required, no endorsement implied); OWID witness = CC-BY-4.0.
notes:
THE SEX DIMENSION (the honest cost of the as-reported route): the DYB collector prints life expectancy at birth for Male and Female separately — there is no "both sexes" column to report, and averaging the two would be a derivation (the canonical tier reports, it does not derive). Every canonical point therefore carries sex="male"|"female" and (entity, year, sex) is the merge key. The OWID witness is both-sexes: it stays comparable at the SERIES level (its both-sexes level sits between the two canonical curves), not pointwise. A both-sexes canonical series would be a derived product, explicitly out of scope until a separate decision says otherwise — and the male/female split is itself a Todd-relevant signal (the Russian sex gap in life expectancy is one of his standing exhibits).
CANONICAL TIER: un_dyb Table 4, editions 2011-2014 + 2017-2024 — as-reported LE at birth over 2007-2024, overlapping windows reconstructed edition by edition, intra-tier arbitration (later vintage wins, logged in provenance.json). Collector holes are data: countries absent from the table's windows (no questionnaire response or no civil-registration LE that year) stay absent. The pre-2007 as-reported history lives in the PDF-era editions — deliberately NOT in this loop (ADR-0007's PDF-route gate).
WITNESS TIER: owid `life-expectancy` — "over the long-run" series combining historical reconstructions (Riley, HMD) with UN WPP estimates, methodologically heterogeneous by period; check n_missing_within_span per country in reports/coverage_report.md before using this series for a given country over a long span.
Life expectancy at 60 (mentioned in the brief as a companion indicator) deliberately absent from this pilot — DYB Table 21 ("Life expectancy at specified ages", latest-year cross-sections, 2005+) is the identified as-reported route; to add in phase 2/3 as a companion indicator.
